Liberal

/LIB-er-uhl/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Something that is liberal is open to new ideas in lieu of traditions.

Her liberal approach to grading rewarded creative, unconventional answers.

Worked Example

A newspaper editor tells her junior reporters that no idea is off the table. She runs experimental story formats, prints unconventional viewpoints, and happily breaks decades-old layout rules whenever a fresh approach serves readers better.

Her defining trait is openness to new ideas instead of loyalty to how things have always been done, which is what liberal describes. Liberal is more precise than 'flexible' because it names a broad willingness to embrace the new over the traditional, not just an ability to adjust.

How Liberal Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

open-minded

open-minded: willing to consider new or different ideas

progressive

progressive: favoring reform and forward-looking methods

tolerant

tolerant: accepting of different views and practices

Antonyms

rigid

rigid: unwilling to bend, adapt, or change

narrow-minded

narrow-minded: refusing to consider other viewpoints

How Strong Is It? — receptive → open-minded → radical → liberal

receptive vs. liberal

receptive vs. liberal: Receptive is weaker than liberal — a receptive listener will hear new ideas out, while a liberal thinker actively welcomes and adopts them.

open-minded vs. liberal

open-minded vs. liberal: Open-minded is slightly weaker than liberal; an open-minded person considers new approaches, but a liberal one is ready to change the rules to make room for them.

radical vs. liberal

radical vs. liberal: Radical is stronger than liberal — a liberal policy loosens tradition's grip, while a radical policy throws tradition out and starts over.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — liber

root — liber: free (Latin)

suffix — -al

suffix — -al: relating to; befitting (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Liber (free) + -al (relating to): liberal originally meant 'befitting a free person' — free in thinking, open to new ideas rather than bound by tradition.

Use the root in a new word: liberty

Use the root in a new word: liberty: The Statue of Liberty welcomes ships entering New York Harbor.

Word Choice

Liberal describes openness to new ideas and a willingness to depart from tradition, especially regarding political or social attitudes (liberal views on reform) — keep it in that temperamental/political register, distinct from unrelated everyday uses like a 'liberal amount' of something.
